How a session works

Three steps, about ten minutes

  1. Pick the motion and your side. Argue for, against, or take a coin toss. Choose Oxford, Lincoln-Douglas, rapid-fire or freeform.
  2. Choose your opponent. A prosecutor, a contrarian, a coach, or a historical figure like Lincoln or Socrates who argues from their documented positions.
  3. Get judged. An impartial judge scores the exchange and picks a winner; the scorecard quotes your weakest moment and a better line.

What makes it useful practice

  • It cross-examines instead of agreeing. Weak evidence gets pressed; a good point gets acknowledged before it is contested.
  • Difficulty changes behavior. Easy is a beatable partner; Hard exploits every gap and concedes only what it cannot answer.
  • Historical figures stay in period. Lincoln will tell you he knows nothing of the year 2026 and drag you back to the motion.
  • The Community Arena. Publish a debate and let others read the transcript and vote on who won: watch public bouts.
  • Related modes. Practice a thesis defense, a public-speaking Q&A, or an expert explaining a topic to a skeptic.

FAQ

Questions, answered

Can I pick which side I argue?

Yes. Argue for, against, or let a coin toss decide. In freeform, no side is fixed.

Is the judge biased?

The judge scores the argument, not the position, and never sees which side you would prefer. The opponent never invents statistics or sources.

Can my class or team use it?

Yes. Schools pay $6 per seat a month with a teacher dashboard that shows scores, not transcripts. Teams pay $15.

What does it cost?

Your first 15 rounds are free with no card. After that: Debater is $12 a month for 300 rounds, Coach is $29 for 750, Champion is $49 for 500 premium rounds plus 60 minutes of photoreal video opponents, and Elite is $100 for 1,000 premium rounds and 2 hours of video. Round packs are $9 for 100, $19 for 250 and $39 for 600, and pack rounds never expire. Teams and departments pay $15 per seat a month, schools $6.
